title: Characterizing universal topological phases beyond spatial embedding
authors: Sunkyu Yu, Xianji Piao, Namkyoo Park
abstract: Although Hamiltonians govern wave-matter interactions, conventional characterizations of topological phases of matter require more than the Hamiltonian alone, relying on global invariants defined on closed reciprocal-space manifolds or local commutation relations with position operators. This spatial dependence precludes a unique characterization of topological phases on an abstract platform, whose Hamiltonian can be defined independently of its spatial embedding. Here we establish a framework for characterizing universal topological phases, grounded in the invariance of topological features under arbitrary Hamiltonian-preserving deformations. We construct a Hamiltonian-based spatial embedding that groups a system's constituents according to their connectivity. This embedding, which reproduces the results of conventional topological diagnostics in established systems, enables a coherent extension of topological phases to complex networks using the Hamiltonian alone, further highlighting exceptional robustness in small-world networks. Our results reshape the conceptual foundations of topological physics by decoupling topological characterization from prescribed physical platforms.
summary: This paper develops a novel, embedding-independent framework to characterize topological phases of matter by deriving spatial coordinates directly from the graph Laplacian eigenstates of the system's Hamiltonian. By applying this method to complex networks, the authors show that topology can be robustly defined even when the physical embedding is arbitrary. This fundamentally shifts the focus of topological physics from geometry to the intrinsic structure of the Hamiltonian itself.
main_problem: Conventional topological phase characterizations depend on the physical spatial embedding, which prevents a unique characterization on abstract platforms defined only by their Hamiltonian.
main_result: The authors propose and demonstrate a Hamiltonian-derived embedding that successfully characterizes topological phases on complex networks, decoupling topology from prescribed physical geometry.
method: They construct a spatial embedding using the lowest-order nontrivial eigenstates of the graph Laplacian, which groups sites based on strong coupling within the Hamiltonian structure.
model_or_system: The work applies to topological phases in various lattices (Hofstadter, kagome, etc.) and extends the framework to complex networks, such as Watts-Strogatz small-world graphs.
key_observables: Local Chern index ($C_L$), local gap ($\mu_L$), and bulk-averaged topological indices ($\langle C_L angle$).
important_parameters: Rewiring probability ($p$) in small-world networks, magnetic flux ($\alpha$), and energy ($E$).
main_assumptions: The Hamiltonian-derived embedding captures phases inherited from local Hamiltonians but may fail to reconstruct all possible topological phases in a complex network.
figures_summary: Figures compare topological diagnostics (like $C_L$) between original and derived embeddings for various lattices, and show the successful recovery of topological features in small-world networks at intermediate rewiring probabilities.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the limitation of embedding-dependent diagnostics, then introduces the Hamiltonian-derived embedding via Laplacian eigenstates, demonstrating its success on canonical lattices, and finally testing its robustness and limitations on complex, engineered networks.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, abstract mathematical tool for defining topological invariants based purely on connectivity and Hamiltonian structure, which is crucial for designing quantum systems on arbitrary or synthetic lattices.
